findings.title: The top-level route does not resolve the added template
findings.body: `topicUnsubscribe` is registered as a top-level route, so Ember will look up its default template under the route name (for example `topic-unsubscribe`), not `topic/unsubscribe`. The added template is registered as `topic/unsubscribe`, which is the name for a nested `topic.unsubscribe` route. Since this route does not set `templateName` or render that template explicitly, navigating from the email link will not render the unsubscribe page and its notification-state control. Rename the template to match the top-level route or explicitly set `templateName: 'topic/unsubscribe'`.

findings.title: A GET request changes a user's notification preference without CSRF protection
findings.body: The new `unsubscribe` action is reached through a GET route and mutates `TopicUser` state. GET requests are not protected by Rails' normal CSRF checks, and this action is also exempted from the XHR check. A third-party page can cause a logged-in user's browser to request `/t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` and silently lower that user's notification level; mail-client/link-preview prefetching can have the same effect. Render a confirmation on GET and perform the mutation via a CSRF-protected POST/PUT (or otherwise use a recipient-bound, deliberate confirmation flow).

findings.title: Unsubscribe bypasses TopicUser's notification-change bookkeeping
findings.body: Saving the `TopicUser` record directly only changes `notification_level`; it does not set `notifications_changed_at`, mark `notifications_reason_id` as `user_changed`, invoke the observer path, or publish the MessageBus notification that other sessions use to refresh their state. In particular, a row whose reason remains `NULL` can later be auto-promoted from muted to tracking by `TopicUser.update_last_read`, because that method treats a NULL reason as eligible for auto-tracking. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user, topic_id, notification_level: ...)` so an explicit unsubscribe remains explicit and connected clients are notified.

findings.title: The shared unsubscribe translation now requires an option MessageBuilder does not default
findings.body: `unsubscribe_link` now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`, but `Email::MessageBuilder` only supplies a default `user_preferences_url`; `unsubscribe_url` is optional and is only added on the notification-mail path in this change. Any existing caller using `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without the new option will raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` while building the text or HTML body, preventing delivery. Preserve the existing builder contract by defaulting `unsubscribe_url`, or use a separate translation/conditional paragraph when no per-topic URL is available.
